faces.f: "I study the past to find hope for the future."

"Any ship that sails on these mean seas for long is bound to pick up a ghost or two."
—Admiral Beckett Brass
"Within every angel is a spirit of light that will fight as long as there is darkness."
"Skill, imagination, smarts: none of it matters unless you have the nerve to use it."
"One knife, two knives, three knives, four—which will drop you to the floor?"
Leaf and soul alike wither at its touch.

"As long as your courage remains, your life will not falter."
—Sephara, Sky's Blade
A circus acrobat in life, she kills with such fluid grace that even her victims are awed by her performance.

"I will make your bones into a weapon that will lay even the mighty low."
—Modriss of Zargoth Fen

"The will to fight and act as one is not limited to a single world. Oketra's teachings are universal."
—Basri Ket

"First, the darkness fell. Terror came next. After that, only despair remained."
—*The Tragedy of Morein*
Liliana inspires horror in many and fanatical admiration in a few.

"Oh, don't be so dramatic. When your eyes bleed, and your brain leaks out your ears, then we'll talk about lost sanity."
—Braids, dementia summoner

"I love those who are eager to serve."
—Liliana Vess
"Quiet in the library" soon gave way to larger concerns.
To the Rakdos, screams of delight and screams of terror are one and the same.
If you feel the ground quake, run. If you hear its bellow, flee. If you see its teeth, it's too late.
Dogs beg. Cats lay claim.
The hunt ends. Lunch begins.
For hydras, most problems can be solved with the addition of a few extra heads.
"Humans bring nothing but suffering and deceit. They are not welcome in my forest."
The elves of Llanowar look to their past to determine the shape of their future.

"Never underestimate the ability of natural forces to adapt to unnatural influences."
—Molimo, maro-sorcerer

"On the eighth day, a blizzard hit. Supplies were lost, and morale plummeted. On the ninth day, Dover found us."
—*To the Summit: A Tale of Survival*
"I have faith in your potential."
When griffins started nesting atop the northern tower, the castellan worried they'd be a nuisance. Instead, they took the entire castle under their protection.
No one is as dedicated to perfection as a stitcher working on their latest masterpiece.

"No owners allowed."
—Sanctuary sign
From here, the path to anywhere may be found.

"All peoples treasure a place where the weary traveler may drink in peace."
—Ajani Goldmane
He will be your loyal champion, and his pack your protectors. All he asks for is a full belly, a spot by the fire, and all the love in your heart.
Emphatic words with powerful gestures. Clearly this was playtime.
He became elder shaman when his predecessor was mysteriously struck by lightning on a cloudless day.
If you're lucky, the centaurs will give a single warning to leave their territory before driving a spear into you. If you're unlucky, the spear is the warning.
"All are welcome in the angels' light."
A unicorn chooses only the most virtuous and noble of knights to be its companion.
It's the favored mount of military commanders as well as anyone with a flair for the dramatic.
Lost at sea doesn't have to mean lost forever.
Fishing boats often follow hunting drakes to find the largest schools of fish.
Basri carries on his god's legacy, spreading her teachings throughout the Multiverse.

"It's contemplative, resourceful, and original. Everything else aside, it's the perfect student."
—Naban, dean of iteration
On the open sea, there is nowhere to hide.
There are still places where a smile and a handshake are all you need to seal a deal.
His crew proudly maintains an accident rate of 100% per day.
"You burn. I'll pillage."

"Bright as any dinosaur—and just as with other great hunters, its colors are a warning."
—Huatli
As the great scourge passed by, Zendikar shivered, then lay silent.
"Arise, great one, and cleanse the world of our enemies!"
Most mirrors show your reflection. Others show your potential.
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Left barren by the Brothers' War, it stands as a stark reminder of Dominaria's likely fate should the Coalition fail.

"Urza fortified every thirty miles on the path to Tomakul, creating a network of trenches the brothers would trade for decades."
—*The Antiquities War*
Between jagged, snowcapped peaks, the dense bands of hardy evergreens provide the perfect cover for roving bands of orc and goblin raiders.
The gate of every kithkin doun is a cunning trap, intended to spill visitors into an oubliette from which there is no escape.
Still to the ignorant eye, yet bursting with life. A million actions and reactions, unstoppable as the dawn.
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.

"Multani's heart is a seed, and all of Yavimaya is its flower. There is as much life here as in the rest of Dominaria together."
—Karn
"Did you bring enough to share with the rest of the class?"
After the invasion, many wanted to leave a life of violence. But once you're a Reckoner, you die a Reckoner.
Worlds apart, Huatli built a device Saheeli would have been proud of.
They called her unique insight a "gift." Then she saw the truth, and suddenly it was a "threat."
"I fight for the suns, the surface, and everything in between."
It leaps from tree to tree, revealing the enemy's positions.

"Vulshok flail, Viridian shield, loxodon blade . . . Tazzir, bring the Moriok hook and assemble the rookies."
—Vy Covalt, Neurok agent
"Phyrexians can't corrupt what they can't get close enough to touch."

"May our blessings sever the tongues of the forsaken."
—Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
After the Battle of Liet Field, the white sun crested above Taj-Nar, bringing hope to all who survived the carnage.
Karn's creation is now his master.

"Perfection is at hand. You have been freed of weakness and made *compleat*."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One

"A true warrior fights with whatever's handy."
—Qerk of the Secret Warren

"The fangren fight without comfort of any kind. We can ask no less of ourselves."
—Tilien, Sylvok partisan

"So, the survivors from Oxid Ridge are on the move. Let them come and witness predation in its purest form."
—Glissa
Her warriors are the last defense against the coming storm.
The squabble over succession was quickly replaced by the struggle to survive.
His crime was silence, and now he suffers it eternally.
"The nim raid our homes without warning. We must defend our homes without hesitation."
No earthly armor is protection against this sweetness.

From time, knowledge.
From knowledge, power.

"The lasting effects are invariably fatal."
—Phyrexian progress notes
Too stupid to survive, too dumb to die.
Freshly promoted to "first rock," Zaz was eager to make an impact.
Malice is appropriate when vengeance is called for.
The best presents are impossible to regift.

"To see past the veil of death, cross it."
—*The Red Book of Mezdrithalik*
Eyeballs that portend unpleasant futures become slimy snacks instead.

"Fire has always been my most faithful companion."
—Jared Carthalion
Telepathy changes minds, necromancy changes lives, but geomancy changes the world.
A mother only a child could love.
She provides marks of protection to those she chooses as family.

"It was difficult to tell whether the piles of gore within their warrens were mere trash heaps, sacred altars, or warnings."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
The tribe was as strong as his longing, their territory as vast as his isolation. The changeling knew he had found a home, and a form.
Pricy baubles are no match for cheap tricks.
Where fickle form meets lasting loyalty.
Whether modeled after bear, bird, or baloth, all claws send the same message.

"He steals power from treasure after treasure, and what does it do for the ouphe? Nothing."
—Jhoira

"Glorious, to walk again across the savannah with my beloved."
—"Love Song of Night and Day"
Fail to respect the forest and you will fertilize it.
The vines overgrew the construct, snapping gears and soaking up aether.
An elephant never forgives.
A forest-wide network of webs brings a hungry couple to captured prey.
Every path leads to discovery.
Forked tails rustled. Talons clicked. A lone sliver streaked overhead like jagged lightning, and the hive thundered.
The call of the sea shapes many souls.
Though the Time of Ice has ended, its relics still slumber in New Argive.
Changelings can't remember where they came from. They just know it wasn't a cradle.
When it finishes the harvest, you'll have nowhere to hide.
There was a time all craven beasts cowered before Avacyn's divine might.

"Within minutes, the strange device was indistinguishable from the other upon my workbench."
—Tocasia, journal entry
The expedition's end began the marsh's story.
When Worzel summoned Segovian angels to fight Thomil's Gargantikari gnats, the ensuing battle numbered among the Multiverse's least destructive.
Two taken, two judged, one returned.
Families of the fallen donate the swords of their loved ones to bolster the city's defenses.

"I don't have time for you right now."
—Teferi

"What cannot be destroyed will be bound, but do try to destroy it the first time."
—Rem Karolus, Blade of the Inquisitors
"Every choice is a joy."
"The patterns of crossing ripples reveal the future to those who know how to read them."
It manifests at wizard academies to siphon inspiration from young prodigies.
"Never leave the future to fate."
Every cry lifts her allies toward the thunder.
It has no respect for the deeds of martyrs, reducing their legacy to a mouthful of flesh.
A mercurial face sows distrust. Distrust reaps a lonely life.
"Why throw away a perfectly good identity?"
Spells of madness often require a sacrifice of sanity.
Some souls yearn to escape death. Others are content to feed the wildlife.
"Who needs imaginary friends when you've got dead ones?"
The more Esper changes, the more he refuses to.
All that's left are broken beliefs.
Everyone wants to be on the winning side.
"No refunds. I cheated you fair and square."

"Beware the gift when you do not know the giver."
—Chulane, Teller of Tales
He protects the fetid bog from light, life, and the hideous sound of laughter.

"Froggy fighter at the gate.
Draw your sword and meet your fate."
—Traditional children's rhyme
The arrival of spring's first flowers is a sacred occasion to Karametra's acolytes, who fill the Setessan woods with song in celebration.

"What do you want to be, now that you're grown up?"
—Yolov, Simic bioengineer
A humble appearance belies a master's skill.
"Through every verdant field, every bough that hangs heavy with fruit, Karametra shows her love."
Automated systems at the Tolarian Academy sort new acquisitions for optimal use, determining which should be studied, eaten, or sold.
Though Heliod turned against humanity in his hunger for power, the ideals he once championed still stand strong.

"Through even our darkest days, we must never cease creating. Each new invention brings value to the world, be it beauty, utility, or both."
—Rashmi, aether-seer
The path to strength is forged in stability.
The path to growth is forged in balance.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — This Saga gains "{T}: Add {C}."
II — This Saga gains "{2}, {T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct artifact creature token with 'This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.'"
III — Search your library for an artifact card with mana cost {0} or {1}, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

faces.f: With one motion, a pest is removed and a scourge inflicted.

"Frankly, destruction is best left to professionals."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage
Even after a false god tore the magic from Dominaria, power still radiated from the Mirari sword that slew her.
It doesn't purr. It hums.
Mood: A friendship that can outlast death.

"Fear not the angels' constant eyes,
E'er on watch from lightless skies;
Eternal vigil will we keep,
Protectors of the Blessed Sleep."
With every end, a new beginning.
The thief doubled back twice, doused herself with perfume, crossed the ocean, and still woke up with her pursuer close on her heels.
The investigator felt a pinch on his ankle. When he looked down, something glittered in the sand.
In the Kathari dumping grounds known as the Boneheaps, its not hard to improvise an offense.
"Ah! Yes! I got its leg to twitch!"
Gisela beheld true divinity, and was humbled.
Ohran mages willingly endure the bites of vipers, believing the snakes bestow great power on those who survive their venom.
It is the warm glow of the setting sun at journey's end, the scent of the evening meal crackling over a fire, and the cacophony of a raucous song shared over tankards of mead. It is freedom.
"I am no sleeper agent. I am a liberator. It is you who are asleep."
"Obey her will! Don't be a fool! Submit your mind to Emrakul!"
Live fully, then return to the beginning.
The Accursed are ever drawn to the Hekma, as though its presence provides a brief respite in their lives of eternal torment.

"Within our minds are limitless depths. Dive down, but don't forget to surface."
—Teferi

"There will come a day so dark you will pray for death. On that day your prayers will be answered."
—Minaldra, the Vizag Atum
"Avacyn's protection is everywhere. From the holy church to the sacred glade, all that we see is under her blessed watch."
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.

"Approach my tower on bended knee or depart from it as ash upon the wind."
—Gadwick, the Wizened
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
On Innistrad, one person's windfall usually starts with another person lying face down in the mud.
All across Gavony, in shuttered bedrooms and locked barns, young people seek the answers their elders failed to provide.
While the Dawnhart witches focus their magic on nature and community, other covens consort with devils and twist the elements to their will.
"Leave behind the sorrow of this body. Be blessed, being of light."
In the adrenaline-fueled chaos, she hadn't even felt the bite.
As werewolf attacks increased, brutal weapons not seen since the Travails were dusted off and put to work.
"Do you smell that, friends? Fear and despair."

n: Arlinn, the Pack's Hope // Arlinn, the Moon's Fury
Dennick, Pious Apprentice // Dennick, Pious Apparition

faces.f: A few weed-choked gourd patches are all that remain of the proud, thriving farms that once blanketed the province.
"Werewolves leave messy trails. Easy to follow. Hard to forget."
Necro-alchemists gained popular support during the Travails, when geist-fueled weapons helped defend towns against mad cultists and Eldrazi monstrosities.
Griselbrand's defeat did not mark the end of the Skirsdag cult. They simply turned their worship to the next demon to emerge from the shadows bearing offers of power.
It herds souls toward eternal torment.
Facets of life, reflections of the soul.

Grieve for the soul in death dishonored.
—Shadow Guild saying

"The foul entities of the Uuserk swamp had never before dared to spread their influence to the very heart of Zhalfir."
—Hakim, Loreweaver

"I do not teach. I simply reveal."
—Daudi, Femeref tutor

There are medicines for all afflictions but idleness.
—Suq'Ata saying

"I shall make walls of their flesh, and their blood will be my mortar."
—Kaervek
Even the lion envies the lark.

"Fetch the pestridder, Paka—we've got dwarves in the rutabagas!"
—Jamul, Femeref farmer
Storyteller: By my hand in the fire, this story is a tale of power. Listeners: May it give you strength.

"Never taunt an embermage, 'What are you going to do about it?'"
—Akin, seasoned askari

The pulsing heat of the midday Sun burns in the Lion's eye.
—Stone inscription, source unknown

My thunder comes before the lightning; my lightning comes before the clouds; my rain dries all the land it touches. What am I?
—Femeref riddle

"Tonight we'll eat a farewell feast. Cold corn porridge is not enough. / Let's peel papayas, pineapples, and mangoes, drink coconut milk, / and bake bananas."
—"Love Song of Night and Day"

"I've never *heard* growth before."
—Gowon, Femeref herder

"I'll capture gentle zebras / for your steeds and fill the stable with every kind of unicorn."
—"Love Song of Night and Day"

From jungle to sea, from sea to stone, from stone to field, from field to bone. What am I?
—Zhalfirin riddle

"The secrets of Phyrexia are expensive. You will pay in brass and bone, steel and sinew."
—Kaervek

"Do not go there, do not go / unless you rise on wings, unless you walk on hooves."
—"Song to the Sun," Femeref song

"When we're aloft, I love to lean over the *Weatherlight*'s railing and watch the patterns the griffins' shadows make on the clouds below."
—Sisay, Captain of the *Weatherlight*
A lie always returns; be careful how you catch it.

"Once, a Quirion asked why I was so cautious when the day was clear. I told him of the sky-blue hide of the cerulean wyvern, and he offered me double if I could conjure a strong tailwind!"
—Sisay, Captain of the *Weatherlight*

"If you weren't born with it, you don't need it."
—Grahilah, former trader of Amiqat

"Quick, Rhirhok—teach me to swim!"
—Makht, goblin casualty

"Comfortable even in a furnace? I've never met one who'd accept my wager."
—Talibah, embermage
Meeting one is definitely the low point of your life.
The sound of every twisted secret tempts you to hear another.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.

"I swear, for every one Prossh devours, three more pop out of a hole somewhere."
—Jaya Ballard
Lush growth spreads like a ferocious blaze across the Otarian hillsides.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
On Otaria, peace and harmony are rare. Places that provide both are cherished.
A figure is moved on a map, and the tide of war changes.
The mizzium-sphere array drove her mind deep into the thought field, where only the rarest motes of genius may be plucked.

"I'd offer your dog a treat, but I'm afraid I don't have any appendages to spare."
—Alquist Proft, to Judith
After the attempt on Aurelia's life, she gave the Agency an ultimatum: solve the case in twenty-four hours, or the Boros Legion would declare war on the Cult of Rakdos.
A reliable, general-purpose toxin is a handy way to save on belt space.
His claws tear at the foundations of civilization.
"Finally, a performance worthy of my applause!"
"'Did I do it?' You'll have to be more specific."

"The emergence of the Eldrazi isn't necessarily a bad thing, as long as you've already lived a fulfilling and complete life without regrets."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
"The changing kind suffers as we do. We must join as one to quench our tyrants!"
The farther he roamed from Jund and its dragons, the more he felt their essence in himself.
A rock between your eyes hurts. A burning rock between your eyes ruins your whole day.

"Down here, we have a more pointed version of the scriptures."
—Urabrask's enforcer
The giant Tarvik dreamed that trinkets and machines caused all the world's woe. When he awoke from his troubled sleep, he took the name Tarvik Relicsmasher.
Mages of Esper measure their wealth and status by the number of servants in their retinues.

"My battle cry reaches ears far keener than yours."
—Saidah, Joraga hunter
It's difficult to outwit something that doesn't speak, strategize, or even think.
She protects the sacred groves from blight, drought, and the Unbeholden.
It eats what it wants to eat—which is anything that moves.
The most successful of Simic creations is cytoplasm, a living, symbiotic substance that feeds off genetic rhythms and strengthens its host in return.

"Where metal is tainted and wood is scarce, we are best armed by faith."
—Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
"We coat ourselves in steel every day. What is etherium but the next logical step?"
Any being that harms them quickly learns its lesson.
With or without witnesses, the suns continued their prismatic dance.

"We thank the souleaters for inscribing our souls with subservience, to reinforce the sacred order."
—Drones' hymn of gratitude

"We will fight as they do: our flesh protected behind metal."
—Tae Aquil, Viridian weaponsmith
At first, vedalken observers thought blinkmoths naturally avoided certain places. Then they realized those places were frogmite feeding grounds.
Structures built from darksteel yield to neither assault nor age.
A symbol of what Mirrodin once was and hope for what it will be again.

"Like dawn's first light, blind the unprepared and banish the shadows."
—Skyhunter creed

"It's easy for the innocent to speak of justice. They seldom feel its terrible power."
—Orim, Samite inquisitor

"The jeweler, the potter, the smith . . . They all imbue a bit of their souls into their creations. The kami destroy that crafted mortal shell and absorb the soul within."
—Noboru, master kitemaker

"The sky teems with just as much life as the forest or the deep seas."
—Hadi Kasten, Calla Dale naturalist

"Your downfall was not your ignorance, your weakness, or your hubris, but your warm blood."
—Heidar, Rimewind master
Hurkyl's research at the College of Lat-Nam wasn't enough to stop the two brothers, but for centuries thereafter her spellcraft taught artificers restraint.
The vedalken interrogate all intruders—once the hoverguards are done with them.
"More of that strange oil . . . It's probably nothing."
Vedalken eyes don't see the beauty in things. They see only what those things can teach.

"This creature is inadequate. Send it to the splicers for innovation."
—Malcator, Executor of Synthesis
Takenuma was filled with a chorus of moans, shrieks, and wails. Some came from the living, some from the dying, and some, most horribly, from the dead.

"You serve Phyrexia. Your pieces would better serve Phyrexia elsewhere."
—Azax-Azog, the Demon Thane
Each Eldrazi ancient spawned a lineage of horrors in unfathomable shapes.
In desolate places, changelings may take the shape of fancies, or memories, or fears.
Even the small wounds let hope bleed out.

"The results of our ninth inoculation were the same. The specimen was, of course, euthanized before the contagion could spread."
—Vedalken research notes
Just as a changeling's influence can have dramatic effects, so too can its sudden withdrawal.

"Look at her, once filled with innocence. Death has a way of wringing away such . . . deficiencies."
—Savra
Bladehold houses a rogues' gallery filled with the living "statues" of the worst enemies of the Auriok.
They'll attack whatever's in front of them—as long as you tell them where that is.
It came as a cruel answer to the farmers' prayers.

"The maaka remain loyal to us in this time of strife. We don't even have to feed them—our enemies do."
—Nedja, Gruul shaman
"Avacyn's protection is everywhere. From the holy church to the sacred glade, all that we see is under her blessed watch."
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.

"Size alone does not guarantee survival."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger

"To those who can hear it, Gaea's battle song brings power as swift as sunlight and as enduring as the deep roots of the forest."
—Gamelen, Citanul elder
When it snared a passing cockatrice, its own soul darkly doubled.
Even what is lost beyond recall returns when coaxed by a dryad's hand.

"The hermit dies. The outcast dies. The lone wolf dies. Only those who stick together survive this world."
—Uros, Pendelhaven elder
Life's circle has become inverted in Grixis. The same energy is endlessly recycled and becomes more stagnant with each pass.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
When the rebels couldn't breach the castle to kill Lalor the Obstinate, they tried a more internal approach to depose the pretender king.

"The Simic come from the cold slow depths. How could they understand the fire in a wild heart?"
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
Each spike is poisoned—the trapmaker's idea of mercy.

Rhox monks are dedicated to spiritual growth and learning, and most bear the sigils of many students. However, they do not gladly suffer fools or those who disagree with their carefully wrought dogma.

"Birth and death are both reversible."
—Nicol Bolas
The vast network of predation on Jund has actually caused some strange creatures to adapt to being eaten.
At his side, humble beasts become weapons more deadly than sharpened steel.

"Esper, like any work of art, can be truly appreciated only from a distance."
—Tezzeret
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.
One of the most ferocious and deadly gargantuans, the thoctar never sees its worshippers, but it often awakens surrounded by gifts and sacrifices.

"Remember by whose gift you ascend."
—Milana, Orzhov prelate
During their endless travels, the mages of the Goma Fada caravan have learned ways to harness both life and death.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
With clarity of vision comes clarity of function.
"One does not question the size or shape of the grains of sand in an hourglass. Nor do I question the temperament of the souls under my guidance."

"You see a bird, an oak, a packbeast. I see the potential for an army."
—Lalia, Selesnya dryad

"Let no child be without a sword. We will all fight, for if we fail, we will certainly all die."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

"What root and branch cannot reach, our winged friends will attend to."
—Zunak, Selesnya strategist
Each monitor is given an eye for each spire it is to guard.
Time is a marvelous plaything.

"I welcome it. The pasture is cleared of weeds and the wolves are frozen solid."
—Lumi, goatherd

"You will fully understand fear when you discover it is the final thing you put your faith in."
—Nicol Bolas
"The essence of a lawful society is swift deterrence."
After the awakening of the Eldrazi, some vampires took it upon themselves to remind the others where their loyalty should lie.
Dark thoughts hatch and twist within the mind, straining to take wing.
"The undead are not 'awakened.' They are evicted when there is no room left in the pit for more bodies."
"Wisdom from the past is best gathered directly from the source."
If there's anything a werewolf hates, it's a collar—especially Avacyn's Collar, the symbol of her church.
Nothing evens the odds like a little lightning.
A goblin raid is a delicate gambit—a blend of stealth, precision, and screaming death.
The larger the crowd, the harder it is for them to run away.
Man's best fungus.
"Beauty determines value, and we determine beauty."
"Beings of the rifts are not natural. No longer will these abominations tread upon the body of Gaea."
The Arbiter is a conduit of justice, a will so disciplined that it dispenses justice without ego or remorse.

"The soul is only as eternal as I say it is."
—Sharuum the Hegemon

"Release that which was never caged."
—Spellbomb inscription

"It contains the wisdom of generations of our people. We permit only a chosen few to don the raiment."
—Imran, Viridian elder
When the School of the Unseen fell, so many magical treasures lay abandoned that no amount of death could deter the stream of thieves and desperate scholars.
One part cunning, one part wise, and many, many parts demented.
The vizier's wisdom proved invaluable in untangling the Mercadian knot of lies.
Like the price of goods, the value of the routes was renegotiated daily.
The touch of his madness can drive anyone into a killing frenzy.
His mind, like his body, is made up of the swamp's flotsam.

"With the proper tools, even the Great River can be dammed."
—Ta-Spon, Cho-Arrim executioner
The crossbow is the ideal weapon for the lazy Mercadians: just point and shoot.
The Cho-Arrim fought Mercadia's decadence with more than just swords.
Starke knew the voice was Takara's, but the venom was Volrath's.
He has the weapons, he has the connections, and he knows the hangar's dark secret.
One fleet was gone; others were poised.

"These guards are the most disciplined military unit in the city. They couldn't fight their way out of a broom closet, but they've got discipline."
—Gerrard, to Sisay
The Cho-Arrim didn't rely only on a secret location to protect their Fountain.
When he's holding the hammers, everything looks like a nail.
Kyren goblins always speak in questions and never allow wrong answers.
With an explosion that shook the foundation of the city, the *Weatherlight* burst from the underground hangar.

"What was heads again?"
—Mercadian magistrate
The masks, like the ancient trees they're grown from, lend strength to the dryads.
As easily as the dryads could close a fist, so could the branches and underbrush entangle.
Just one can feed a dozen people for a month.
Deepwood's reach is not long, so it invites its enemies in.
They stay on the battlefield only long enough to consume the losers.
"The River flows. My soul returns."

If the ground is smooth, the way will be rough.
—Deepwood saying
It hardly weighs anything, but it takes all day to remove.
Mercadian soldiers excel at finding things to stand behind.
Once you learn to float on the shadows, you'll never fear them again.
